proof: Assign A the reflection f(x)=-x and B the reflection g(x)=2-x. Both are involutions. A noncrossing perfect matching contains an adjacent matched pair; remove it and induct. Every such matched word must compose to identity, hence send 0 to 0. All ten input words send 0 to nonzero values, so none can have such a matching. This is a necessary-condition proof independent of the candidate stack implementation.
